What does it cost to install carpet in Newcastle, WA?

Plan on $4 to $7 per square foot installed, which covers the carpet, the pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. Most Newcastle projects total $2,000 to $4,500, and a 1,200 sq ft main floor with a staircase typically finishes between $5,500 and $8,500. Grade of carpet swings the price more than anything else — and you choose it from full-size samples laid out in your own house.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come to Newcastle?

It does — Newcastle is home turf for us. The van arrives with 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades, we set samples down in the actual rooms so the color reads true in your own light, measure everything including the stairs, and leave a written price before the visit ends. No store trip anywhere in it, and the appointment costs nothing.
What does carpet stretching cost in Newcastle?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Newcastle. A power stretcher pulls ripples, waves and bunched spots flat again for roughly a fifth of what new carpet costs — the smart repair whenever the pile still stands up and you still like what's on the floor.
How much are carpeted stairs in a Newcastle home?

Stair carpet starts at $18 per step, installed waterfall or cap-and-band. Newcastle's 90s two-stories are full of switchback landings and pie-shaped winder steps, so we count every one in the written quote from the start — nothing surfaces later as an add-on.
How long does a carpet install take in Newcastle?

One day handles most Newcastle houses. Three or four bedrooms plus the staircase is a normal day for the crew; a whole house with heavy furniture and long stair runs can carry into a second day. Your quote spells out the schedule, so there's no guessing on install morning.
Will your installers move my furniture?

Yes — the big pieces are on us. Beds, dressers, couches and tables get moved and set back where they belong once the carpet is in. Your part is the small stuff: closet floors, electronics, lamps, breakables and anything personal you'd rather carry yourself.
Is my carpet worth restretching, or should I replace it?

Restretch when the backing is sound, the pile springs back and the color still suits the room — a $99-per-room repair instead of a new floor. Replace when traffic lanes stay matted, seams are letting go, the backing crackles, or pet odor returns after a professional clean. We tell you honestly which side yours falls on before we quote anything.
Which Newcastle neighborhoods does the van cover?

All of them — Hazelwood, China Creek, Newcastle Highlands, Olympus, the Lake Boren area, May Creek and the streets up the Cougar Mountain flank, plus Coalfield next door. We also run to the neighbors: Newport Hills, Factoria, Somerset, Lakemont, Kennydale and the Renton Highlands, with Bellevue, Renton and the wider Eastside in easy range.
What carpet stands up best to pets?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, laid over a moisture-barrier pad. The backing and barrier keep accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber can take cleaning as strong as diluted bleach without losing color. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot and earns its keep the first accident.
What warranty comes with the install?

OC Flooring covers the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet carries the mill's own wear-and-stain warranty on top — usually 10 to 25 years depending on grade. Both go in writing on your quote. Worth knowing: some mill warranties require a minimum pad grade, which is one more reason all three grades come along on the visit.
